original.target_description: Karraker and DeLamater (2013), older opposite-sex married NSHAP respondents, sexual inactivity. Multiple candidate predictors/models/comparisons at supplied page; target test unresolved.

notes: Primary title verified; PDF pp. 10–13 rendered and inspected. Study/description are absent; locator supplies only a page, with no predictor, model or contrast. Page interpreted as PDF/article-relative p. 10 or 11 (printed pp. 151/152); printed journal pp. 10/11 are absent. No target assigned by audit ID, row order or numeric matching. Candidate sample evidence only: Missing Data (printed p. 148/PDF p. 7) identifies 1,502 married respondents (889 men, 613 women), 637,092 person-months, 53,091 person-years. Analytic Approach (printed p. 149/PDF p. 8) explicitly identifies person-month as unit of analysis; Table 3 repeats these roles. Of 1,801 married respondents, 299 excluded: 217 missing last-sex year, 21 other marriage-history information, 61 covariates. Table 1 has pooled and gender-specific descriptives; Table 2 n = 1,462 with age counts 620, 533, 309 excludes missing sexual frequency for some active respondents. Common model counts are candidates for parent field-scope review, not assigned analytic N. No N sums or metric conversions performed. PDF p. 11 contains Table 2 and many pooled Table 3 tests. Printed Model 6 OR candidates: duration 1.18; respondent physical health 0.59; partner physical health .75 (narrative 0.75); partner mental health .89 (narrative 0.89); respondent age 1.16; partner age 1.13; remarriage .18; premarital cohabitation .86; spouse-age categories .18, .89, .53, 1.54. These are distinct coefficients, each triple-star (p < .001), Table 3 PDF pp. 12–13. Respondent mental health Model 6 OR 1.00 has no star or exact printed p. Earlier models provide further candidates. Table 3 prints husband age category 6–11 years whereas narrative/Table 1 say 6–10; discrepancy retained. Target predictor/model/contrast remains unknown. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
